description: Represents a data table as ONE unit: a row/column grid, OR a long uniform serial/itemized catalogue (an appendix/schedule/serial list of many same-shape entries). Standalone or embedded, single-page or continuing across pages.
applicability: The content is a grid of rows and columns.

OR it is a long, uniform, parallel-structured serial/catalogue list (many same-shape numbered or bulleted entries forming a catalogue/appendix/schedule) — that is a table even when it visually reads as a list.
The table may stand alone or be referenced by nearby text, and may continue onto the next page.
instructions: Emit the table as ONE block of block_type table. Prefer STRUCTURED content: headers + rows (a list of cells per row).

Do NOT shred a data table or a uniform serial catalogue into many text_block items — a long serial appendix/schedule list is ONE table, not dozens of blocks, EVEN when the OCR renders it as a markdown/HTML list.

Keep sub-items and their aligned values within their own row/cell; do not explode a multi-value cell into separate rows. A row of bare ordinals under the real headers is column numbering — treat it as header, not data.

If the table spans pages, treat all fragments as ONE table: reuse the SAME stitch_id across fragments, do not repeat the header row as data, and ignore any running header/page number that interrupts it.
Attach the table to the block that introduces/references it via parent_block_id when there is a clear reference; otherwise leave parent_block_id null.
Distinguish a data grid / serial catalogue (this skill) from a genuine bulleted/numbered list (list skill) or running prose (text_block).

provenance.reason: General-document adaptation (MPDocBench): generalized the legal table skill (v1) for any-domain tables; kept the long-uniform-list-as-table rule that the schedule-guard retrieval relies on.
